fix(auth): keep verified same-account session rotations and report refresh failures accurately

Contract v1 for open issue #19 and an observed misdiagnosis in this public skill. Base main 371df78fd47b515e83eb54f19fbc8b340e460d16 (if advanced verify ancestry and no overlapping repair). One bounded writer. Read AGENTS.md, DECISIONS.md, applicable SKILL.md. No provider account access, model submissions, cross-host transfers, new endpoints, browser credential extraction, challenge or anti-abuse logic. Offline synthetic fixtures only.

Reproduce #19 with a failing fixture: verifying an already saved, still valid, same-account session can accept legitimate server-issued rotation but return success without persisting it. Use the existing auth lock, fresh re-read under lock, existing verified state serialization/permissions and atomic write semantics. Save only verified changed state, keep unchanged content/time, preserve a concurrent newer session, and keep account-binding, failure-preservation and existing normal renewal behavior. No broader credential discovery, no changes to the browser trust boundary, no periodic services, and do not overwrite an active user's auth on verification failure.

The current renewal code also maps malformed JSON, absent, expired, or unparseable token responses to one message claiming revocation. The observed public symptom class is an HTTP 200 session response containing an explicit service RefreshAccessTokenError and an unusable access token. Implement precise fail-closed sanitized classification at the existing validation boundary so a real refresh rejection calls for same-account sign-in, a service/schema/invalid-token problem calls for technical diagnosis, and an unauthenticated empty session is represented accurately. Never echo raw provider response text, unknown error values, tokens or identity. Distinguish failures with focused regression fixtures and keep successful paths and saved-job semantics intact. Do not claim the persistence defect caused any particular live rejection. No changes to model quota, polling, or automatic generation budgets. If useful, add a short targeted troubleshooting sentence to the skill's existing auth section. Do not edit unrelated issues.

Run exact repository gates including deno check, deno test --allow-read --allow-write .agents/skills/gpt-pro/tests/, targeted lint/format, git diff --check and repository verify as applicable. Return exact base, commit, tree, commands/pass counts, what reproduced on base, and uncertainties; include the evidence in the final message itself. No additional jobs, deployments, or production access. Estimated 10-18 minutes.
